title: Narada
shortDescription: A self-correcting agentic search pipeline that researches any topic and hands back a table of facts, each one linked straight back to its source, and searches again to fill any gaps.
description:
Narada takes a research topic and returns a structured table of facts, each value linked back to the page it came from. When the first pass leaves gaps, it runs targeted follow-up searches to fill them instead of stopping there.

It runs as a **self-correcting agentic pipeline** in Python/FastAPI: scrapes the web concurrently, uses **LLM extraction** to turn pages into structured entity data (reading **schema.org** data directly when a page already has it, skipping the LLM call), dedupes across sources by fuzzy name match, and computes a **completeness score** to decide whether another search round is worth running. The loop is capped so a sparse query doesn't run forever. Includes a **43-test pytest suite**.

Source traceability is enforced at the **Pydantic data model** layer. Every extracted value carries its source URL, quote, and confidence, so an unsourced value can't exist, and a conflict between two sources resolves by which one the model was actually more confident in, not an arbitrary tiebreak.

The LLM layer runs on **LiteLLM** as a provider-agnostic interface, swappable through config with per-step model overrides and automatic failover across **5+ LLM providers and 3 search providers**. Even the public demo runs a **zero-server-side-secret** architecture: user-supplied API keys travel as per-request headers and are never stored server-side.

title: Atlas
shortDescription: A distributed ride matching system that pairs riders with nearby drivers in real time, and keeps matching correctly and fast even while part of the infrastructure is actively crashing mid-request.
description:
A rider requesting a ride needs a fast, fair match, even if part of the system is failing mid-request. Atlas proves that match still happens correctly and quickly regardless.

Three independently deployable services communicate over **gRPC**/Protocol Buffers: dispatch-service (orchestrator), pricing-service (pure calculator), and trip-service (system of record, its own **MySQL** schema), each containerized with **Docker**. Matching runs a **two-stage pipeline**: a **grid-bucket index** narrows candidates, then an ephemeral **quad-tree** ranks them in logarithmic time, feeding a **lookahead algorithm** that scores drivers on projected time-to-pickup. Real road distance comes from **OSRM**, with automatic fallback to haversine math on failure.

Deployed to **Kubernetes**, fault tolerance was proven by killing a live pod mid-load-test: failure rate held at **0.2-0.4%** with zero cascading restarts. Trip requests write a durable REQUESTED row before matching starts, so a crash mid-match stays recoverable. A **non-blocking OSRM client** with a fail-fast admission gate isolated the real throughput constraint to external OSRM latency (**1.4-1.9s**), not app-side sizing, and explicit gRPC deadlines cut worst-case failure time from 120+ seconds to under 1 second.

title: RiskWise
shortDescription: A maritime risk intelligence platform that analyzes live world events, scores shipping routes, and suggests safer alternatives when risk is too high.
description:
RiskWise answers the question a logistics team actually asks before committing to a route: is this safe right now. Give it a route like Shanghai to Rotterdam and it returns a risk score, a plain-language explanation, and a safer alternative if the numbers say you need one.

Three specialized **LLM agents** split the work. **Athena** gathers what's actually disrupting that specific route from **3 live public sources in parallel** (NASA EONET, USGS Earthquakes, GDELT). **Hermes** scores the risk across **4 independent factors**: weather, labor, geopolitical, congestion. **Apollo** generates a safer alternative if the score crosses threshold.

A **cascading fallback system** (live sources, then database, then LLM synthesis) means the system never returns nothing, even when external APIs are down. The frontend is a **4-page React dashboard** with **MapLibre GL JS** route visualization, a live agent terminal, a threat feed, and trend history, running on **tRPC** and **Drizzle ORM** over PostgreSQL.

title: Donna
shortDescription: An AI executive assistant that books appointments, handles reschedules, and messages clients for service businesses through a multi-agent orchestration system.
description:
Donna handles scheduling, reschedules meetings when plans change, and messages clients directly to keep them in the loop. Book a call, need to move it, cancel last minute: Donna manages that conversation so the business owner doesn't have to.

It's built as a **multi-agent system** in Python/FastAPI: a **central orchestrator** manages the business owner's side, while an **isolated agent spawns per client conversation**, so no client's context ever bleeds into another's and scheduling conflicts get resolved automatically.

Every database mutation (booking, rescheduling, cancellation) runs through a **typed MCP tool layer** before it touches anything real, with an in-process agent registry and **Redis**-backed conversation state. A **two-stage LLM firewall** screens inbound messages for prompt injection and outbound messages for hallucinated bookings, and an **LLM judge** decides whether a message gets handled autonomously, flagged to the admin, or escalated.

title: Heimdall
shortDescription: An AI wholesale order assistant that checks customers, stock, and costs before handing a human a draft to review and approve.
description:
A wholesale inquiry looks simple but hides real judgment: is this buyer legit, can the order ship from current stock, what does a shortfall cost. Heimdall does that judgment automatically and hands a human a draft to approve.

Built on Google's **Agent Development Kit (ADK)** running **Gemini**, gated on both ends by callbacks: a **before-model callback** redacts PII and screens for prompt injection before the LLM ever sees the input, and an **after-model callback** re-scans the draft output for leaked PII and auto-send language. The agent calls **4 read-only MCP tools over stdio** for customer, inventory, and production-cost lookups, so it has no direct database access.

The reasoning chain computes `shortfall = max(0, (DTC velocity + wholesale ask) - stock)` and branches into production-cost estimation when supply falls short. Human-in-the-loop is a **structural guarantee**, not a prompt instruction: every MCP tool is read-only, so there's no code path to an auto-sent message. Backed by a **41-test suite** and was deployed to Google Cloud Run.

title: Clinical Copilot
shortDescription: An AI clinical chart analysis tool that turns raw patient notes into a structured chart review, with red flags and a medication check.
description:
Clinical Copilot turns a pile of raw patient notes into something a clinician can actually use: a structured SOAP note, a red-flag list, and a medication check, generated in seconds instead of an afternoon.

A **6-agent pipeline** in Python/FastAPI runs the analysis, with **deterministic fallback extraction** built into every agent, so the system still returns clinically usable output even if the LLM call fails. **Medication and timeline agents run in parallel**, with risk and synthesis sequenced downstream.

Medication data gets enriched through the **OpenFDA drug label API** for real interaction lookups, not just text summarization. **W&B Weave observability** wraps every agent call, and a single analysis run produces **two reports** from the same data: a clinician-facing structured version and a plain-language patient-facing one.

title: Deepfake Deconstruction
shortDescription: A deep learning pipeline that traces a face-swapped deepfake photo back to the original source image it was built from, instead of just flagging that it's fake.
description:
Most deepfake tools stop at 'this is fake.' This one goes a step further and traces a face-swapped image back to the actual source photo it was built from.

A **modular deep learning pipeline** built in Python/PyTorch, using **convolutional architectures** with feature extraction layers designed so individual components can be swapped without touching the rest of the pipeline.

Tested against a **custom dataset of 10,000+ manipulated images**, identifying the original source image with **85%+ accuracy**. The goal was to treat deepfakes as an **AI safety problem** worth tracing to its origin, not just a detection problem worth flagging.

title: Stroke Biomarker Extraction
shortDescription: An ML pipeline that extracts movement biomarkers from wrist-accelerometer data to predict stroke-recovery outcomes, and measures which parts of a pretrained movement model's output can actually be trusted.
description:
Wrist trackers are cheap and always worn, so if the movement signal they capture carries real clinical signal, stroke recovery could be monitored without a clinic visit. This project measures how much of that signal a pretrained movement model actually captures, and which parts of its output are reliable enough to trust.

Raw wrist-accelerometer recordings across **61 subjects** and **587,046 windows** are preprocessed into per-visit HDF5 files, then run through a frozen pretrained **transformer** (**Bio-PM**) to produce **1028-d embeddings** per clinical visit. Three extraction-pipeline variants were built across windowing and token-pooling strategies, including a corrected masked-pooling path after finding the model's original pooling averaged over NaN-padded slots.

**Leave-one-subject-out** Ridge regression against continuous ARAT and FMA clinical scores shows the **128-d accelerometer sub-stream alone** predicts impairment better (**R2 approx 0.56**) than the full 1028-d vector (**approx 0.49**), with the unusable 900-d gravity sub-stream root-caused to a **DC-removal artifact** in the source data. A per-dimension **ICC reliability** screen isolates 125 to 127 of 1028 dimensions as stable, all in the accelerometer sub-stream. Graduate course project (CS690R, digital biomarkers, UMass Amherst), built with a team of 3.

title: DKeeper
shortDescription: A decentralized note taking app that stores notes on the Internet Computer blockchain without relying on a traditional backend server.
description:
DKeeper is a note-taking app built to keep working even if the usual thing behind every app, a server, goes away.

A **React** frontend calls a **Motoko** backend canister directly on the **Internet Computer** through generated **Candid bindings**, with no REST API and no backend server in between. Every note is persisted in **canister stable memory**, so data survives canister upgrades without a database.

Type safety runs end to end: **TypeScript bindings** are generated straight from the canister's typed Candid interface, so frontend and backend types can't drift apart.

title: File Vault
shortDescription: A personal file hosting service that lets users upload, download, and delete files while enforcing ownership on every request.
description:
File Vault is a personal file hosting service: upload, download, or delete a file, and only the account that owns it can touch it.

A **React** SPA talks to an **Express/TypeScript API** backed by **MongoDB**, checking ownership on every file route before anything happens to it.

File access is hardened against **path traversal** with a filename allowlist and a resolved-path boundary check, paired with **bcrypt** password hashing and a MongoDB-backed session store. Uploads use UUID-prefixed storage with filename sanitization at write time.

title: URL Shortener
shortDescription: A URL shortener that turns long links into unique short codes while preventing duplicate entries and unsafe URL schemes.
description:
URL Shortener does exactly what it says, and does the one thing most clones get wrong: submit the same long URL twice and you get the same short code back, not a duplicate.

A **Node.js/Express/TypeScript** API generates **nanoid**-based short codes backed by **MongoDB**, with deduplication baked into the write path.

Every submitted URL is checked against an **http/https protocol allowlist** to block javascript: and other XSS-prone schemes, and short-code uniqueness is enforced at the **database layer** with a unique index and a single automatic retry on collision.
